description: GOSTrocks is a Python library of support functions used by the World Bank Geospatial Operations Support Team for routine geospatial preparation: raster clipping and zonal statistics, summarising gridded population such as WorldPop or GHSL over administrative units, urbanisation extents and similar tasks, with example notebooks. The team produces it to standardise the data preparation behind World Bank exposure, urbanisation and service analyses. Coverage is global and resolution follows the rasters and vector layers the user supplies. Access is by pip install GOSTRocks, with a function reference and a usage primer on the documentation site. Licence: Mozilla Public License as stated on the documentation; the library is free. Caveats: it is a collection of helpers, not a single documented workflow, the page notes that pip holds the most recent stable version while source builds come later, and no version history was read. It supports hazard exposure and resilience studies by turning population and hazard rasters into unit-level inputs. Related catalogue records are WorldPop and the Copernicus GHSL built-up and population layers it is commonly run on, and GOSTnets from the same team.
